name: Clinic sessions
summary: Consulting rooms booked out in half-day sessions, with clinicians who are only available for some of them.
when_to_choose: Choose this if your day is divided into morning and afternoon clinics rather than shifts, the limit is how many rooms you have, and each clinician works a fixed number of sessions a week.

knobs.label: Days in the clinic cycle
knobs.help: Five for a pattern that repeats every week. Ten if some clinics run only on alternate weeks.

knobs.label: Length of one session
knobs.help: In minutes. A hundred and eighty is a standard half-day clinic; shorter sessions let you fit more into a day.

knobs.label: Consulting rooms available
knobs.help: How many rooms can run a clinic at the same time. This is usually the real limit on how much you can book.

knobs.label: Sessions in a day
knobs.help: Two means a morning and an afternoon clinic. Three means you also run an evening or an early list.

questions: How many clinics do you run, and what is each one called?
How many consulting rooms can be in use at the same time?
How many sessions does each clinician work in a week?
Are there sessions that need a particular room - a procedure room, one with equipment in it?
Does anything have to happen on a fixed day, such as a weekly multidisciplinary meeting?
tradeoffs: Shorter sessions fit more clinics into the same rooms, but every extra changeover costs time and the room is never quite empty when the next list starts.
Letting a clinic use any free room fills the building more evenly, but a clinic that always sits in the same room keeps its equipment and its notes where the staff expect them.
Protecting a whole session a week for administration is what stops clinics overrunning into the evening; it also costs you a room and a clinician that the waiting list would happily have used.
